source_text: וַ/יַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת הַ/יָּ֖ם מוּצָ֑ק עֶ֣שֶׂר בָּ֠/אַמָּה מִ/שְּׂפָת֨/וֹ עַד שְׂפָת֜/וֹ עָגֹ֣ל סָבִ֗יב וְ/חָמֵ֤שׁ בָּֽ/אַמָּה֙ קוֹמָת֔/וֹ ו/קוה שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים בָּֽ/אַמָּ֔ה יָסֹ֥ב אֹת֖/וֹ סָבִֽיב־־׀׃
english_snapshot: Then he made the cast sea[a], ten cubits from brim to brim, round all around; its height was five cubits[c][b], and a line of thirty cubits went around it all around.

signals.text: The written form here is קוה ('line'), traditionally read with the sense of measuring cord; compare the parallel in 2 Chronicles 4:2.

source_text: וְ/הַ/בַּ֤יִת הַ/זֶּה֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה עֶלְי֔וֹן כָּל עֹבֵ֥ר עָלָ֖י/ו יִשֹּׁ֣ם וְ/שָׁרָ֑ק וְ/אָמְר֗וּ עַל מֶ֨ה עָשָׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ כָּ֔כָה לָ/אָ֥רֶץ הַ/זֹּ֖את וְ/לַ/בַּ֥יִת הַ/זֶּֽה־־׃
english_snapshot: And this house will become a ruin[a]. Everyone who passes by it will be appalled and will whistle, and they will say[b], ‘Why has Yahweh done thus to this land and to this house?’

signals.text: Hebrew: 'this house will be high/exalted.' In context, many understand the sense to be that it will become a ruin or object of horror; compare 2 Chronicles 7:21.

source_text: וְ/אֶֽת בַּעֲלָ֛ת וְ/אֶת תמר בַּ/מִּדְבָּ֖ר בָּ/אָֽרֶץ־־׃
english_snapshot: and Baalath[a], and Tamar in the wilderness, in the land.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'Tamar'; the parallel passage in 2 Chronicles 8:4 reads 'Tadmor.'

source_text: וְ/נָבִ֤יא אֶחָד֙ זָקֵ֔ן יֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּ/בֵֽית אֵ֑ל וַ/יָּב֣וֹא בְנ֡/וֹ וַ/יְסַפֶּר ל֣/וֹ אֶת כָּל הַ/מַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה֩ אִישׁ הָ/אֱלֹהִ֨ים הַ/יּ֜וֹם בְּ/בֵֽית אֵ֗ל אֶת הַ/דְּבָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר אֶל הַ/מֶּ֔לֶךְ וַֽ/יְסַפְּר֖וּ/ם לַ/אֲבִי/הֶֽם־־־־־־׀־־־׃
english_snapshot: An old prophet was living in Bethel[a], and his sons came and told him all the deed that the man of God had done that day in Bethel, and the words that he had spoken to the king[b]; they told them to their father.

signals.text: Hebrew shifts from singular ('his son came and told him') to plural ('they told them to their father'). This may imply more than one son or reflect a textual/narrative irregularity; the translation preserves the shift rather than harmonizing it.

source_text: וַ/יֹּ֗אמֶר לֹ֥א אוּכַ֛ל לָ/שׁ֥וּב אִתָּ֖/ךְ וְ/לָ/ב֣וֹא אִתָּ֑/ךְ וְ/לֹֽא אֹ֣כַל לֶ֗חֶם וְ/לֹֽא אֶשְׁתֶּ֤ה אִתְּ/ךָ֙ מַ֔יִם בַּ/מָּק֖וֹם הַ/זֶּֽה־־׃
english_snapshot: And he said[a], “I cannot return with you or go with you, and I will not eat bread or drink water with you in this place.”

signals.text: The Hebrew uses a feminine 'with you' in the first two clauses and a masculine 'with you' in the eating and drinking clause. English does not preserve this gender distinction.
